import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.83

by V. P. Shunkov

Suppose that $G$ is a periodic $p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite group which
has a finite Sylow $p$-subgroup. Are all Sylow $p$-subgroups of $G$ conjugate?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.83»

/-- A group $G$ is $p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite if, for every finite
subgroup $H$ of $G$, any two conjugate elements of order $p$ in
$N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Subgroup G), Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      orderOf x = p → orderOf y = p → IsConj x y →
        Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/--
For every prime $p$, suppose that $G$ is a periodic $p$-conjugacy
biprimitively finite group and that at least one Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$ is
finite. Is it true that every two Sylow $p$-subgroups of $G$ are conjugate in
$G$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.83» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      Monoid.IsTorsion G → IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite p G →
      (∃ P : Sylow p G, Finite P) →
      ∀ P Q : Sylow p G, ∃ g : G, g • P = Q := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.83»
modeling_decisions: Interpreted the parenthetical “periodic” as the hypothesis `Monoid.IsTorsion G`, i.e. every element of `G` has finite order.

Defined Shunkov's `p`-conjugacy biprimitively finite condition using the standard quotient `H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer`; for conjugate quotient elements `x,y` of exact order `p`, their generated subgroup is `Subgroup.closure {x, y}` and finiteness is `Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})`.
Expressed “has a finite Sylow p-subgroup” existentially as `∃ P : Sylow p G, Finite P`.
Expressed pairwise conjugacy of Sylow subgroups via Mathlib's conjugation action as `∀ P Q : Sylow p G, ∃ g : G, g • P = Q`.
Quantified universally over natural primes `p`, as specified by the decomposition table.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.83

by V. P. Shunkov

Suppose that $G$ is a (periodic) $p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite group (see 6.59)
which has a finite Sylow $p$-subgroup. Is it then true that all Sylow $p$-subgroups
of $G$ are conjugate?

Following Problem 6.59 (V. P. Shunkov), a group $G$ is called *$p$-conjugacy biprimitively
finite* if, for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$, any two conjugate elements of order $p$
in the quotient group $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup.

Here a Sylow $p$-subgroup of a (possibly infinite) group is a maximal $p$-subgroup,
as in Mathlib's `Sylow p G`.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.83»

/--
A group $G$ is *$p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite* (V. P. Shunkov, see Problem 6.59 of the
Kourovka Notebook) if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$, any two conjugate elements of
order $p$ in the quotient group $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup.

Since conjugate elements have the same order, it suffices to require that one of the two
elements has order $p$.
-/
def IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      orderOf x = p → IsConj x y → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- Every finite group is $p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite, for every $p$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite_of_finite (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite p G :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ _ => inferInstance

/--
Suppose that $G$ is a periodic $p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite group (see 6.59)
which has a finite Sylow $p$-subgroup. Is it then true that all Sylow $p$-subgroups
of $G$ are conjugate?

Here $p$ is any prime, a Sylow $p$-subgroup is a maximal $p$-subgroup (`Sylow p G`),
"has a finite Sylow $p$-subgroup" means that at least one Sylow $p$-subgroup is finite,
and "all Sylow $p$-subgroups are conjugate" is expressed as the transitivity of the
conjugation action of $G$ on `Sylow p G`, i.e. for all Sylow $p$-subgroups $P, Q$ there is
$g \in G$ with $g P g^{-1} = Q$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.83» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Monoid.IsTorsion G →
      IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite p G → (∃ P : Sylow p G, Finite P) →
        MulAction.IsPretransitive G (Sylow p G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.83»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The table's single-slot reading (∀ p prime, periodic p-conjugacy biprimitively finite G with some finite Sylow p-subgroup ⇒ all Sylow p-subgroups conjugate) and its definition of Shunkov's notion match the statement and Problem 6.59.
modeling_decisions: 'p-conjugacy biprimitively finite' is formalized as: ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H → ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer, orderOf x = p → IsConj x y → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y}). The quotient is the quotient group N_G(H)/H (Group instance via Subgroup.normal_in_normalizer, verified). The order-p condition is imposed only on x, since y is conjugate to x and hence automatically has order p; this is noted in the docstring.
The parenthetical '(periodic)' is taken as a genuine hypothesis `Monoid.IsTorsion G` (every element has finite order), as instructed by the decomposition table.

'Sylow p-subgroup' is Mathlib's `Sylow p G` (maximal p-subgroup, valid for infinite groups); 'has a finite Sylow p-subgroup' is existential: `∃ P : Sylow p G, Finite P` (verified to elaborate as finiteness of the carrier of P.toSubgroup). Sylow p G is always nonempty (⊥ extends to a maximal p-subgroup), so the hypothesis is not vacuous.

'All Sylow p-subgroups of G are conjugate' is `MulAction.IsPretransitive G (Sylow p G)`, Mathlib's own phrasing of Sylow's second theorem (`Sylow.isPretransitive_of_finite`). Verified with #synth that the instance is `Sylow.mulAction` (conjugation, `g • P = MulAut.conj g • P`, i.e. x ∈ g • P ↔ g⁻¹ x g ∈ P), and that IsPretransitive unfolds to ∀ P Q, ∃ g, g • P = Q.

p is universally quantified over primes (`∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → …`), since the problem does not fix a particular prime; G ranges over `Type` (universe 0), following the sibling Kourovka files (1_40, 19_25, 20_76).
A small `@[category test]` lemma (every finite group is p-conjugacy biprimitively finite) is included as basic API for the bespoke definition, per CONTRIBUTING.md; it is proved by `inferInstance`.

The definition is kept in the problem file (not FormalConjecturesForMathlib) since it is specific to Shunkov's Kourovka problems; a reviewer may prefer to move it to FormalConjecturesForMathlib if Problem 6.59 is also formalized.

Built from existing primitives `Subgroup.normalizer`, `Subgroup.subgroupOf`, `QuotientGroup`, `orderOf`, `IsConj`, `Subgroup.closure`, `Finite`.
